chunks: And as for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:

The mu'lli (husband who makes a vow of abstention from his wife) is compelled to divorce with a single irrevocable divorce. This narration does not contradict the first narration in that he has the right of revocation (raj'ah) for it, because this narration is marfu' (stopped) and not musnad (connected to an Imam), because Mansur ibn Hazim gave a fatwa and did not connect it to any of the Imams (peace be upon them). It is permissible that this was his opinion, even if it was mistaken. And if he had connected it to some of the Imams (peace be upon them), the narration could be understood as referring to one who sees that the Imam compels him to divorce with a single irrevocable divorce by separating her and then divorcing her. Or the narration could be specific to one whose wife is with him on a single divorce, for indeed the ruling for one in this state is that his divorce becomes irrevocable.

key_terms.أَمْلَكَ بِرَجْعَتِهَا: He has the right of revocation (raj'ah)
key_terms.الْمُؤْلِيَ: The husband who makes a vow of abstention from his wife
key_terms.مَوْقُوفَةٌ: Stopped narration (attributed to a successor, not the Prophet or Imam)
key_terms.مُسْنَدَةٍ: Connected narration (attributed directly to the Prophet or Imam)
key_terms.يُبَارِيَهَا: He separates from her (consummates or separates)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on compulsion to divorce for a husband who makes a vow of abstention (ila') according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi analyzes the chain of transmission to distinguish between a definitive ruling from the Imams and the independent juristic opinion (ijtihad) of Mansur ibn Hazim, who is cited as having 'given a fatwa' rather than narrating directly from an Imam. This scholarly distinction allows for the reconciliation of apparent contradictions by interpreting the 'compelled irrevocable divorce' as either a specific application for those with one prior divorce or as a probable juristic view that may contain error, highlighting the nuanced methodology of hadith verification in Shia fiqh.
